title: When the Homecoming Burns
premise: Freya Iversen has spent three years at Ashford High keeping her head down, channeling everything she can't say into the bread she bakes in her late mother's kitchen. When her history teacher pairs her with Wren Calloway — the girl whose family's bakery chain gutted Freya's father's shop, and who once humiliated her in front of the whole school — for a semester project on local food heritage, both girls are trapped: pass or fail graduation together. Their research forces them to uncover that their families' feud hides a shared, buried history neither parent ever told them, and as they train for the county baking championship they've been dared to enter, rivalry curdles into something like trust. At the championship, Freya must choose between winning on her own terms and exposing the truth that could save both bakeries; she loses the title but wins back her voice, and the two of them rebuild what was burned — one loaf, and one honest conversation, at a time.
about_author: Silas Yarrow is a former line cook turned high school substitute teacher who writes stories about kids who feel too much and say too little. They live above a bakery, which they insist is a coincidence.

chapters.title: The Careful Girl
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. We meet Freya kneading grief and silence into sourdough before dawn, navigating school as an expert of invisibility three years after her mother's death and her family's public humiliation by Calloway's Bakery. The chapter ends when Mr. Okafor announces semester pairings and reads 'Iversen and Calloway' aloud to a room that goes very quiet. Emotional beat: dread cracking open routine.

chapters.title: What the Recipe Cards Knew
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Forced to interview their own parents for the heritage project, Freya and Wren discover contradictions: a decades-old recipe card in Freya's mother's handwriting bearing the Calloway name, and Wren's grandmother's letters hinting the two families were once partners, not rivals. A hostile library session turns into reluctant collaboration. Emotional beat: suspicion giving way to shared curiosity neither will admit.

chapters.title: Proofing
chapters.summary: Wren's POV, then Freya's. Dared by classmates to enter the county championship, the girls train together through failures and small confessions — Wren reveals the humiliation was staged by her older brother protecting a family secret; Freya admits she stopped speaking up the day her mother died. They find proof the Calloways bought the Iversen bakery under pressure from a developer, not greed. Emotional beat: trust rising like dough, fragile and warm.

chapters.title: When the Homecoming Burns
chapters.summary: Both POVs converge. At the championship, held during homecoming weekend, Freya presents their joint entry — the recovered partnership recipe — and publicly tells the truth instead of playing safe, forfeiting the judges' favor. The crowd, including both families, hears it all. Her father and Wren's grandmother reconcile over the original ovens; Freya and Wren walk out titleless but unhidden. Emotional beat: burning down invisibility and finding identity in the ashes.
